operator_request: Implement WP-006 without mockups or vibe coding, use the already-open logged-in Firefox only when a live canary materially helps, use subagents for adversarial implementation review through different lenses, harden the work, and address findings, gaps, concerns, ROI, and bad code hygiene.

Source-level solver, seven upstream player families, nine player variants, n/sig test vectors, and generated release assets were inspected.

current_primary_sources.evidence: Pure-Rust engine source, context isolation, instruction budget, loop/recursion/stack limits, feature surface, tests, and maintenance activity were inspected.
RuntimeLimits exposes loop-iteration, recursion, stack, and backtrace bounds; context construction also exposes an instruction budget.

current_primary_sources.identity: current source and nova_vm 1.0.0 publication inspected
current_primary_sources.evidence: Nova remains a less mature engine with broader unsafe/GC surface and no demonstrated yt-dlp EJS corpus compatibility; it is not selected for this bounded spike.

selected_approach: Use boa_engine 0.21.1 with default features disabled inside a policy-marked non-shipped Rust executable worker.
Execute the exact pinned yt-dlp-ejs 0.8.0 generated library and core assets plus pinned upstream player scripts, not handwritten challenge lookalikes.
Use WP-005 ff.javascript-worker@1 envelopes and Ferric length-prefixed frame validation at the parent/worker boundary.
Create a new Boa Context for every job and expose no host network, filesystem, environment, process, console, or secret APIs.
Enforce input, output, frame, instruction, loop, recursion, stack, wall-time, job-count, age, and RSS/recycle bounds; use parent process supervision for non-cooperative timeout and cancellation.
Emit deterministic per-case reports and an aggregate PASS_RUST_ONLY_PATH or FAILED_SPIKE_REQUIRES_OPERATOR_DECISION verdict.
rejected_options: Deno, Node.js, Bun, QuickJS, QuickJS-NG, Wasmtime, rusty_v8, Hermes, or another external/native runtime because the Operator and packet forbid them.
Nova for this spike because current maturity and corpus evidence are weaker and its unsafe GC surface adds risk without a demonstrated compatibility advantage.
A handwritten JavaScript subset or Rust reimplementation of challenge transforms because it would be a mock of the actual EJS execution requirement.
Network-downloading EJS/player assets during build or test because it violates deterministic offline proof and the no-build-download boundary.
Treating generic Test262 or simple eval success as YouTube challenge compatibility proof.
reuse_opportunities: Reuse the existing locked Cargo workspace, architecture policy, report envelope, scanner, negative-fixture harness, and canonical gates.
Reuse WP-005 JavaScriptWorkerEnvelope, FrameDecoder, ProtocolLimits, typed failure codes, cancellation generations, and state-machine identities.
Reuse WP-004 pinned yt-dlp identity and provenance conventions while adding the missing EJS/player corpus under WP-006.
Reuse Rust std process, pipe, timing, hashing, and filesystem APIs plus already-approved serde/serde_json/sha2 before adding any new mechanism.
basis.validation_plan: Run exact pinned corpus cases through a spawned Rust worker; inspect reports; run malformed/partial/oversized/protocol/cancel/timeout/crash/memory/capability/cache/context/recycle/quarantine probes; scan dependency, source, build scripts, artifacts, process plans, FFI, links, and downloads; run format/check/test/doc/Clippy/architecture/deep/PR gates; then rotate independent subagents through engine-security, protocol-lifecycle, corpus-proof, and code-quality attack lenses, convert every confirmed finding into a public-boundary regression, remediate, simplify, and rerun the complete matrix.

assumptions: The pinned yt-dlp 2026.07.04 release and yt-dlp-ejs 0.8.0 assets remain the packet baseline even if upstream moves during implementation.
A passing spike selects a prerequisite mechanism only and is not a video downloader or product capability.
The logged-in Firefox session is optional live-canary context and is never a source of committed cookies, tokens, secrets, or deterministic corpus truth.
non_goals: Downloading the requested Short, implementing the YouTube extractor, or claiming full YouTube support.
Shipping the worker or granting it network/filesystem/process capabilities.
Adding an external runtime, Python, yt-dlp product execution, Wasm, or a new native dependency.

corpus_contract.mandatory_cases: Every pinned case in the checked-in WP-006 manifest; the manifest is derived from the upstream 0.8.0 tests and binds player bytes, variant, challenge type, input, expected output, EJS asset hashes, and upstream commits.
corpus_contract.pass_threshold: 100 percent exact output agreement for mandatory deterministic cases, with no skipped or structurally-only cases.
corpus_contract.live_canary_policy: Optional, non-blocking, separately labeled, sanitized, and never allowed to replace deterministic corpus proof.
corpus_contract.failure_bundle: Case ID, upstream identities, script/player hashes, engine identity, bounded non-secret input, expected and observed result, typed error, limits, duration, process/RSS observation, and replay command.

resource_and_security_contract.capabilities: No registered network, filesystem, environment, process, dynamic import, module loader, console, timer, or secret-bearing host functions.
resource_and_security_contract.isolation: Fresh Boa Context per job; host-owned content-addressed artifacts; no durable JavaScript heap or global state across jobs.
resource_and_security_contract.termination: Engine budgets are cooperative first-line controls; parent wall deadline/cancellation may terminate and reap the separate worker. Timeout is a bounded policy outcome, not proof that arbitrary code could never finish.
resource_and_security_contract.memory: Input/output and engine structural limits are exact; parent RSS supervision provides bounded detection and forced worker termination. The report must state OS hard-containment coverage and residual race/overshoot rather than claim a perfect in-engine heap cap.

minimum_controls: Real pinned EJS and player bytes execute through Boa and an output mutation fails the same oracle.
Every worker request crosses the bounded public frame/envelope boundary and receives a correlated typed terminal outcome.
Parent supervision proves termination and reap for infinite loop, cancellation, crash, malformed stream, timeout, and memory pressure.
Dependency and source scans reject all forbidden runtimes, downloads, FFI, native links, and indirect wrappers.
No PASS is possible with skipped mandatory cases, missing process proof, structural-only behavioral evidence, or a positive product-progress claim.

execution_decomposition: Commit activation, refinement, zero-progress ceiling, and exact checkpoint.
Add the pinned offline EJS/player corpus and a behavior-sensitive manifest validator.
Implement the non-shipped Boa worker, bounded envelope/frame protocol, fresh-context execution, and parent supervisor.
Implement typed report/verdict generation and capability, bounds, lifecycle, cache, churn, dependency, and counterfactual probes.
Run multi-lens independent adversarial reviews, remediate every confirmed finding, simplify, and rerun all acceptance and canonical gates.
